_read_me: Measurement pass of everything the current pack places, before the Towns-and-Towers/Dungeons-and-Taverns re-skin. All offsets are [dx,dy,dz] from the Town Anchor (VALLEY.OFF in valley_core.js) unless marked HOME-relative. A 'mark' name is a key in VALLEY.OFF, resolved at runtime via v.mark(name) = anchor + OFF[name] (or v.home() for 'home'). Every finale/scene command list is itself written as ~ offsets from its own origin mark, resolved by valley_finales.js resolve(). Ranges below are that mark's local ~ offsets, so 'absolute anchor offset' = OFF[origin] + local range.

home.note: NOT an OFF entry — separate persistentData key valley_home, set by Q2 waystone placement on the Kettle ruin hearthstone. Everything HOME_* is relative to this, not to anchor.

ruin.note: valley_ruin — the Kettle ruin hearthstone placed at first join by setup/place_ruin.mcfunction, offset from the player's actual spawn/house pick, NOT a fixed anchor offset. Home is normally set on top of it.

inn.desc: The Hearth / centre of the 9x9 inn shell built by scene 'inn' (valley:act1/inn_shell) at Q8. MOVED here from the old [-14,1,4] (which collided with the granary) — comment says this is the only mark every dependent quest addresses by name, never a literal coordinate.

mill.desc: The mill / Bram's shell + race, built by scene 'bram' (valley:act1/bram_arrives) at Q12

granary.desc: granary_shell placed by finaleAct2, granary_facade + noticeboard placed by finaleAct3

lake.desc: The Pier waystone; basin dug and pier placed by finaleAct2

echo_cave.desc: probe-only mark, BOX.echo_cave=[8,6,8], no build found placing terrain here — it is assumed to exist naturally / from world stage 'act5' content not covered in these three files

home_relative_marks.note: Q5 gate: flatDist(player,home)<=16 && player.y <= home.y-3. Q55 gate (only after world stage act3): flatDist<=10 && player.y <= home.y-6. Q90 (the bare 40th lamp post): must land within 2 blocks of home+HOME_PORCH; force-set lit the instant it's placed.

lamp_road.engine_note: A LAMPS_* array entry is the POST's own y (the fence); the LAMP block itself is stored/placed at y+LAMP_HEAD(1). persistentData.lamps[] always stores the LAMP coordinate. Act IV's lever sweep and the /valley scene q74 sparkle both iterate v.lamps().
lamp_road.count_check: 4 + 2 + 4 + 17 = 27 whitelisted anchor-relative posts, + Wisp's 4 unlisted river posts (scene q58, never counted) + 4 reed-village-adjacent (n/a) + the Q90 home-porch post (40th) + bathhouse's 2 (scene q72 'also') + Halden-still's lantern (not a road post) = the 40 total the bossbar/board text claims. Exact 40th accounting: 4+2+4+17=27 road posts + q90's 1 = 28 counted-in-persistentData whitelisted-or-Q90 posts; scene q58 (4), q72-also (2) and bram/marnie/pip/nesting_box/cottage/square_path/cellar's incidental fence+lantern posts are cosmetic lanterns, NOT createdeco lamps, so they never enter v.lamps() at all — only LAMP_BLOCK (createdeco:yellow_copper_lamp) placements do. VERIFY against valley_checks.js before touching any of these arrays.

hard_constraints_the_redesign_must_keep: Every quest/probe in valley_checks.js reads v.mark(<name>) or v.home()/v.anchor() at RUN TIME — so a rebuild that changes what /valley scene <key> or finaleActN place, but keeps the SAME anchor-relative OFF[] coordinates (or moves an OFF[] value and updates every consumer in lockstep across valley_core.js + valley_finales.js + valley_checks.js), preserves every probe automatically. Renaming or shrinking a mark's OFF entry without touching all three files breaks quests silently.

LAMPS_FINALE / LAMPS_Q07 / LAMPS_Q34 / LAMPS_Q74 are baked into BOTH valley_core.js (VALLEY.C) and valley_finales.js (the POST/LAMP_LIT/LAMP_DARK constants + literal command arrays) — changing lamp-post positions means editing both files identically, and the actual placed LAMP_BLOCK positions must land inside LAMP_TOLERANCE (2 blocks) of the whitelisted array, or Q34/Q74 never complete and the Act IV lever never finds them.

The Works chamber MUST stay a sealed shell before being dug out (WORKS_SHELL: walls first, floor+ceiling, THEN air+water-replace) — anchor+[34,-6,-20] is 6 blocks underground and any redesign that digs air before sealing risks flooding from any nearby aquifer/lake/river again.

The inn mark (anchor+[-8,1,12]) must stay clear of: the mill house (x -24..-16, z 2..10), the granary (x -14..-6, z -4..4), the town square paving (x >= -7 only above z 7), the bathhouse + its posts (x <= -15), the Act V town hall (z <= -7), and the Act V approach path (x -2..2). This footprint math must be redone from scratch for whatever Towns-and-Towers 'tavern' piece replaces it.

The lake basin (finaleAct2) is a DUG, SEALED basin (stone shell + 5 water-replace plugs) — not natural terrain — because the Act II 'Float' needs open, controllable water at a known absolute location for the raft-lantern/lily-pad scatter and the pier template. Any new pier/lake structure needs the same dig-and-seal treatment or a lakeside/coastal anchor can drain the basin.

The noticeboard's sign text is written via `data merge block`, never `setblock`, because a `place template` (or a hand-built equivalent) leaves an oak_sign at a position whose blockstate already matches what setblock would write — an identical setblock silently drops the NBT. Any replacement noticeboard structure must be placed FIRST, then have its sign text applied with `data merge block` as a separate step.

square_path.mcfunction's two LAMPS_Q07 posts and finaleAct1's four LAMPS_FINALE posts are the 'six lamps burning' the Q19 quest text and Oda's Act II line both count literally — a redesign of the town square must still leave exactly these six anchor-relative positions (or their v.lamps()-registered equivalents) lit from Act I onward.

HOME_CELLAR_Y (-3) and HOME_DEEP_Y (-6) are absolute vertical gates off home.y — any new cellar/cottage template must still put its cellar floor at home.y-6 or below (with a mid-landing at home.y-3) or Q5/Q55 stop firing.

HOME_PORCH ([3,0,0] off home) is where Q90's 40th lamp force-lights the instant a createdeco:yellow_copper_lamp lands within 2 blocks — a new cottage template needs a bare fence-post-sized gap at this exact offset (or the offset must be updated in valley_core.js and nowhere else, since nothing else reads it).

Q47 (energy duct) and Q70a (beds) and Q73 (chair) and Q60/Act IV's Hearth-relight and Q18's chalked spots all address the SAME `inn` mark and its local wall-relative offsets — a new inn structure must keep the Hearth roughly centred with a back wall the mill-facing/square-facing side, since Q18's three chalk spots are 'the back wall' (south) and the beds are 'the west wall'.

finaleAct4's forceload radius (FORCE_R=40) around works/anchor/inn/bathhouse must still cover every mark any new structure touches, or a finale claimed from far away will silently build nothing (runCommandSilent returns 0, logged as a warning, never surfaced to the player).

excavateWorks() is called from BOTH q65's scene and finaleAct4's beat0, and is idempotent via v.once('works_excavated') — a re-skinned Works interior must preserve this single shared latch, not add a second independent dig.

Every NPC import position (bram at mill+[11,1,2], marnie at cottage-local [0,1,7], pip at inn-local[0,1,3]→[-5,-1,4] via scene, oda/pip/marnie/bram at anchor±4 for the Fair, tobin at the outcrop then the square, nella at the lake then the Float, wisp at the lake shore, the four ribbits at anchor-relative spots then works, the three newcomers on the Act V approach path) uses a DETERMINISTIC preset UUID, so a re-import at a new coordinate MOVES the resident rather than duplicating them — any redesign that changes a building's footprint just needs to update the npc(...) coordinate in the same scene/finale function, nothing else has to change.

The Q65/Q71 lever cell (works+[0,2,0] on a wall panel at works+[0,2,-1]) is the exact block Act IV's finale later sets POWERED — a new Works layout must keep a wall at that relative offset for the lever to mount on, or it pops off as an item the next time a neighbour updates.
